subject: EmbedFlow ops check-in: integration fit, SDK changes & next steps
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@medicore.com>, Priya Sengupta <priya.s@medicore.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: EmbedFlow ops check-in: integration fit, SDK changes & next steps

Thanks again for your time this morning, Alex & Priya — good discussion. Quick recap from Redwood on the operational and integration points we agreed were top of mind, plus proposed next steps.

High-level pain & goals (as we heard them)
- Retrieval/embedding scale: large corpus (200k+ clinical notes) with low-latency reranking for triage UI (target median latency <= 400ms in-prod).
- Structured outputs: clinician-facing summaries must adhere to a fixed JSON schema (fields: summary, severity_score, recommended_action).
- Streaming + partial results: UI wants token-by-token partial summary streaming while reranker finalizes top candidates.
- Cost constraints: budget-conscious on per-request token spend; interested in caching + lower-dim embeddings for cold queries.

Integration & product fit notes
- SDK: plan to add a streaming hook and a function-calling shim so you can receive partial JSON fragments as they arrive and validate against your schema client-side.
- Function calling / structured output: we will map Redwood function-call responses to your JSON schema; Ben will provide an example function signature.
- Embeddings & rerank: recommend starting with our embed-rerank-v2 family (quantized variant available); we will provide a small evaluation set for tuning dimension vs. latency/cost tradeoffs.
- Autoscaling / capacity: for the scale you described we recommend Redwood Dedicated with an initial reserved pool and a small burst lane to protect latency SLAs.

Immediate asks from MediCore
1) Shared sample dataset (500 representative notes) + an example of the UI flow where streaming is expected.
2) Procurement contact for MSA/po paperwork (Priya, can you confirm?).
3) Any SSO/SAML onboarding doc or environment we can test against.

Proposed next steps
- Ben to post a short implementation note (SDK changes + example function signature) by EOD today.
- We schedule a 60-min technical POC kickoff next week to validate streaming + rerank on a small slice of your corpus. Suggested slots: Tue/Wed 11/10–11/11, 10am–1pm PT.
- Provide sample dataset and UI spec by end of week so we can prototype the streaming behavior.

Attachments: embedflow-proposed-scope.pdf (outline of scope and success criteria).

If we missed anything or misstated priorities please flag — otherwise I’ll track action items and send calendar invites.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com

Vanessa — thanks for the clear recap. This matches our read on the call. A couple of clarifications from our side:  

1) Sample data: we can extract and share ~500 de-identified notes by EOD Thursday. Will deliver as newline-delimited JSON.
2) Latency targets: our product team would be happy if median end-to-end (client -> embed + rerank -> client) is <= 300–350ms for top-K=5 on our average 120-token queries. Is that realistic with the quantized embed-rerank you mentioned?
3) Procurement: Priya is copied — she is our procurement lead. Priya, please add details for MSA and proc timelines.

Looking forward to Ben’s implementation note. We’re generally excited about streaming partial summaries, that will be a big UX win.

—Alex
Alex Turner
Senior Product Manager | MediCore Health
alex.turner@medicore.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@medicore.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: EmbedFlow ops check-in: integration fit, SDK changes & next steps

Thanks — quick technical response to Alex’s latency question and the SDK/implementation approach. Quoting Vanessa’s original recap below for context.

On achievable latency
- For median end-to-end 300–350ms on top-K=5 for 120-token queries: possible on dedicated capacity with the following configuration:
  * Dedicated instance pool (A100-class or equivalent) with per-tenant KV cache for hot prefixes.
  * Use embed-rerank-v2-quant (low-bit quantization) for embeddings to reduce memory and compute; pair with a small, local approximate nearest neighbor index per-tenant.
  * Continuous batching disabled for interactive path; we’ll use low-latency route with small batch size (1–4).
- Expect median ~150–300ms in our benchmarks for similar workloads; p95 will depend on query complexity and index hit-rate. We’ll instrument and provide token-level breakdowns via the Console.

SDK & function-calling work
- I’ll attach a patch (sdk-change-patch.diff) that adds: streaming callbacks, a function-call shim that emits validated JSON fragments, and a helper for gradual reassembly of partial structured outputs in the browser.
- Example function signature (high level):
  {"name": "generate_clinical_summary", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"summary": {"type": "string"}, "severity_score": {"type": "number"}, "recommended_action": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["summary"]}}

Workplan & risk notes
- Short POC: integrate SDK streaming hooks + run a 1k-query rerank evaluation to tune embedding dim vs cost. Target: 2 sprints of engineering (internal) + 1 joint week of testing.
- Risk: if your/our index warm-up is poor, p95 latency could spike. Mitigation: small caching layer and pre-warm during peak windows.

I’ll upload the patch and a runnable POC container image to the Drive link Vanessa shared. Happy to do a code walkthrough during the kickoff.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@medicore.com>, Priya Sengupta <priya.s@medicore.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 15:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: EmbedFlow ops check-in: integration fit, SDK changes & next steps

Great — thanks Alex & Ben for the quick responses. Confirming action items and next steps: 

1) MediCore: share 500 de-identified notes (NDJSON) and UI streaming spec by EOD Thu 11/12 — Alex/Priya.
2) Priya: please share procurement contact and estimated PO timeline so we can align onboarding.
3) Ben: upload sdk-change-patch.diff and POC container to the Drive link and drop a short README with run steps (target: today).
4) I’ll send a calendar invite for the POC kickoff — proposed Tue 11/10 at 10:30am PT (please accept or propose alt).

Meeting link: https://meet.google.com/lookup/medicore-embedflow-call
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/7842
Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aB2cEmbedFlowScope

If everyone is aligned I’ll also open a short Jira for the POC (RDW-7842) and attach acceptance criteria. Anything else to add?

Thanks — looking forward to the kickoff.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
